Commentary.Commentary: Right then, it's been a damp and disappointing start to the Super Six stage here in Sarawak. We have one more game scheduled at this venue later in the day at 6.30 am GMT between South Africa and Ireland. However, given the forecast for the rest of the day and the current ground conditions, stars will need to align for any action to take place. For now, feel free to switch tabs and catch the action from the other Super Six game currently underway between the USA and New Zealand. After being asked to bat first, New Zealand have been bowled out for just 97. The USA will fancy their chances of gunning down this total, setting up an interesting chase. See you there. Cheers!

UPDATE - 3.51 am GMT - The official word is in - The game has been ABANDONED. This outcome was expected, given the overnight rain and the persistent drizzle since the morning. With this outcome, both teams collect one point each to kickstart their Super Six campaign.

UPDATE - 3.33 am GMT - The drizzle continues, with puddles visibly forming on the covers. On the lighter side, Nigeria's players are keeping spirits high with some lively dancing, while the English players are staying loose by engaging in a game of keepy-ups. It's a waiting game, but at least there's some entertainment on the sidelines. As previously mentioned, the forecast predicts rain throughout the day, and later today, South Africa and Ireland are set to play here as well. However, conditions will need to improve significantly for any action to take place.

UPDATE - 3.20 am GMT - Not much has changed here in Sarawak as we continue to wait for the rain to relent. Meanwhile, over in Bangi, things have taken a dramatic turn for New Zealand. After an encouraging start at 32/0, they have now slipped to 55/6, losing 6 wickets for just 23 runs. A lot is unfolding there, so switch tabs and catch the action!

The race for the final spot went down to the wire in the 2022-2025 ICC Women’s Championship, with New Zealand edging past Bangladesh due to a higher number of wins (nine compared to Bangladesh’s eight). Both teams finished with 21 points in the 10-team tournament, where each side played eight three-match series, split equally between home and away fixtures. With this result, New Zealand joined Australia, England, South Africa, Sri Lanka, and the hosts, India, in securing direct World Cup entries. Bangladesh, West Indies, Pakistan, Scotland, Thailand, and Ireland will compete in the World Cup Qualifier later in the year, with two spots for the main event up for grabs.

In other news, New Zealand have secured the last direct qualification spot for the ICC Women’s ODI World Cup 2025 following Bangladesh’s defeat in the final game of their ICC Women’s Championship series against the West Indies in Basseterre.

While we wait for the situation to improve here in Sarawak, you can switch tabs and head over to Bangi, where the USA and New Zealand are battling it out in one of the four Super Six clashes scheduled for today. New Zealand have been inserted into bat, and more importantly, the weather in Bangi is clear with blue skies, making it ideal conditions for cricket!

Charlotte Lambert of England is also up for a quick chat. She says they all have the same passion for the game and enjoy it very much. Adds that they all have bonded very well on this tour and that they back each other. Says that the biggest challenge is playing in rainy conditions like you have to set up a target and with the DLS situation, it becomes difficult at times. Talks about the preparation, and says that the team does make strategies before each game and they make decisions based on that. Tells that they keep it simple and back each other's strengths to come out on top.
Nigeria's Deborah Bassey is in for a chat. She says that their unity is their biggest strength. Mentions that the World Cup has given her an opportunity to showcase her talent.

UPDATE - 2.16 am GMT - Oh, no! We should have had the toss by now but it is currently raining at the Borneo Cricket Ground. As a result, the flip of the coin has been DELAYED. The entire ground is under cover, and we can only hope the weather clears up soon to get things underway. Charles Dagnall informs us that Sarawak has experienced a lot of rain over the past couple of days and adds that the forecast doesn't look too promising. Fingers crossed for some action!

The pitch at Sarawak has offered good bounce and assistance for bowlers, but batters who are willing to spend time in the middle have also reaped rewards. We can expect another gripping battle between bat and ball today. While England will look to assert their dominance, Nigeria’s fearless approach makes them a dangerous opposition. It promises to be a riveting contest with plenty of fireworks on display. Stay tuned!

Nigeria, meanwhile, stunned everyone with their memorable win over a strong New Zealand side, proving they are not just here to make up the numbers. Skipper Piety Lucky has been inspirational with her all-round contributions. For Nigeria to challenge a strong English side side, they’ll need their entire squad to deliver under pressure.

England come into this contest with confidence, having secured two dominant wins to top Group B. Their bowlers have been the backbone of their success, showcasing sharp discipline and variation to trouble opposition batters. However, their batting lineup, while effective, has shown signs of vulnerability, which could be an area of concern. Davina Perrin will hold the key for them at the top of the order.

Hello and welcome to the Super Six stage of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025! Today, we’re in for an exciting showdown as England Women Under-19 take on Nigeria Women Under-19 at the scenic Borneo Cricket Ground in Sarawak. Both teams have displayed moments of brilliance in the group stage and will now look to step up their game as the competition gets tougher.

It's time for the Super Six leg of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup, 2025, and in Match 2, we have an intriguing clash lined up as Group B toppers, England Women Under-19, face off against Group C's second-place holders, Nigeria Women Under-19. This contest is set to unfold at the picturesque Borneo Cricket Ground in Sarawak. England enters this game with the momentum of two commanding victories after their opening game was washed out by rain. Their bowling unit has been nothing short of exceptional, with both pacers and spinners proving to be consistent troublemakers for opposition batters. However, their batting unit has shown a few chinks, which they’ll aim to iron out as the competition intensifies. The in-form Davina Perrin and Trudy Johnson have been the backbone of their scoring efforts, while wicketkeeper Katie Jones has been a standout, not just with her electrifying work behind the stumps but also with crucial contribution in high-pressure situations. With most boxes ticked England will look to deliver a collective performance and bring their A-game. On the other hand, Nigeria Women Under-19, after a washed-out opener, turned heads with a sensational victory over New Zealand, a result that has fueled their confidence heading into this stage. While they couldn’t sustain their momentum and fell to South Africa in their final group game, they’ve shown they have what it takes to challenge strong teams. Skipper Piety Lucky has led from the front, excelling with both bat and ball, while Lilian Ude has been a pivotal figure in the side’s scoring. However, for Nigeria to stand toe-to-toe with England, it will require a cohesive team effort, with every player stepping up to the challenge. With England holding the edge on paper, the scales seem tilted firmly in their favour. However, Nigeria’s fearless spirit and knack for springing surprises make this an enticing matchup. Could we witness another giant-killing act in this edition, or will England’s might prove too much to handle? We shall very soon find out.
